title: scitex-live-paper evidence report
description: What an evidence provider supplies to scitex-live-paper: one entry per REGISTERED claim with its evidence state, a one-line reason, its source and locator, and its minimal evidence graph. Text that is not a registered claim never appears. Versioned by schema_version (semver): a MINOR bump only adds optional fields; a MAJOR bump changes or removes fields. See docs/evidence-provider-contract.md.

state.description: supported: the stated value was checked against its source and the source against its recorded computation, and both hold. not_supported: something the provider checked does not hold (reason says what). not_checkable: registered and connected, but the value itself could not be checked (e.g. no locator). no_evidence_graph: registered, but no recorded computation connects it to a source.

file.description: Manuscript file, relative to project_root (or absolute).

stated_text.description: The claim's text as written in the manuscript.

stated_value.description: The value the claim states, any JSON type.

reason.description: One plain-language line a reviewer can act on.

locator.description: Where in the source the value lives (provider-defined shape), or null.

value.description: Added in 1.2.0. The value the provider read at the locator, any JSON type. Omit the key when the provider did not read one (a null value means the source holds null).

provider_status.description: The provider's own raw verdict, opaque to scitex-live-paper (shown verbatim).

graph.description: Minimal evidence graph. Omit the key to have scitex-live-paper ask the provider on demand; null means the claim has no graph.

failure.description: Added in 1.1.0. Marks a graph node where the evidence broke. kind is a short token; changed (content differs from what the recorded computation saw), missing (absent), and mismatched (holds a value other than the claim states) are the recommended ones, and a consumer shows any other token verbatim. detail is one plain-language line.

summary.description: One line describing the graph (e.g. how it was reduced).
